source_admission: Primary publications and agency guidance, with exact reading/access limits. External PDFs remain in temporary storage; no external dataset or complete paper is redistributed. Literature results, conservation calculations and proposed industrial applications remain distinct.

sources.title: JSC 29353D: Flammability Configuration Analysis for Spacecraft Applications
sources.reading_scope: Revision history; sections 5.1 and 5.2, printed pages 11–13; selected assembly and battery passages. PDF text retrieved; no complete handbook or current standard audit.
sources.use: Oxygen and diluent partial pressures both matter; limited partial-gravity coverage; components that pass separately can fail in an assembly. No lunar material acceptance inferred.

sources.title: Oxygen Partial Pressure and Oxygen Concentration Flammability: Can They Be Correlated?
sources.reading_scope: Methods, compiled pressure/composition findings, conclusions and Table 2 read. Table 2 on PDF page 15 rendered and inspected. Proposed reaction-site explanation read but not adopted as established kinetics. No audit of every underlying experiment.
sources.use: Compiled upward flame propagation/self-extinguishment evidence reaches 119.3 kPa for some materials; composition can dominate near normoxic conditions. Supports a material-specific atmospheric advantage, not 121.59 kPa lunar qualification.

sources.title: Ventilation Effects on Compartment Fire Characterization
sources.reading_scope: Abstract, experimental setup, oxygen profiles, burning-rate discussion and conclusions read. Printed page 411 (PDF page 9) rendered; Equation 2 inspected. Not every figure or test record reviewed.
sources.use: Audit of the inherited 0.65 burning-rate bracket; original normalized correlation uses oxygen at the flame base and is not a general law for a new pressure/gravity.

sources.title: Pressure Effects on Oxygen Concentration Flammability Thresholds of Materials for Aerospace Applications
sources.reading_scope: Abstract, methods, material list and pressure range read from primary PDF text; no table-image inspection.
sources.use: Earlier polymer/elastomer tests at 48.2, 85.3 and 101.3 kPa; pressure dependence and material dependence, without 1.2 atm lunar data.

sources.title: Partial gravity flammability of cast PMMA rods in concurrent axial stagnation flow
sources.reading_scope: Indexed primary publisher abstract, highlights and experimental-setup excerpt read. Direct page retrieval returned 403. Full paper, images and supplements unexamined.
sources.use: Cast PMMA tests at 0.04–1 g, 13.2–15.2% O2 and average 57.6 kPa found maximum flammability near lunar gravity. Different atmosphere and geometry from industrial production.

sources.title: The Effect of Gravity on Flame Spread over PMMA Cylinders
sources.reading_scope: Primary full-text methods, results, discussion and conclusion passages read; no supplementary data or figure-image review.
sources.use: Low opposed-flow ISS tests distinguish slower spread from lower extinction limits, with nonmonotonic flow effects. Array freefall does not supply a universal safer comparison.

sources.title: The combined effect of pressure and oxygen concentration on piloted ignition of a solid combustible
sources.reading_scope: Primary PDF abstract and introduction read. Full experimental methods, figures and numerical fits not reviewed.
sources.use: Subatmospheric PMMA piloted ignition shows nonmonotonic pressure response; ignition cannot be inferred from propagation tests or oxygen fraction alone.

sources.title: Overview of dust explosibility characteristics
sources.reading_scope: Primary agency record and PDF text sections 4.4–4.7 on oxygen, temperature, pressure and hybrid mixtures obtained through web retrieval. Local PDF download returned 403; local bytes/hash and figures unverified. Web extraction uses an incorrect display title; the agency catalogue and PDF first page identify Cashdollar correctly. Claims restricted to obtained text.
sources.use: Dust-specific oxygen/pressure/size/temperature effects and coal propagation below 17.5%; neither dust control nor explosion severity follows from polymer screening.

sources.title: Improving Process Heating System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, Second Edition
sources.reading_scope: Indexed primary text of Appendix B Tip Sheet 3, printed page 71, read. No full handbook review.
sources.use: Nitrogen carries sensible heat into exhaust; oxygen enrichment can improve high-temperature heat delivery, requiring its own cost account.

sources.title: Alternative Control Techniques Document: NOx Emissions from Process Heaters
sources.reading_scope: Primary indexed thermal-NOx mechanism passage on printed page 4-2 read; no complete emissions-model or regulatory review.
sources.use: Thermal NOx depends on flame temperature, oxygen, nitrogen and residence time. Added nitrogen is not an automatic emissions reduction.

sources.title: Advanced Combustion
sources.reading_scope: Agency web description of nitrogen removal, CO2-rich exhaust and oxygen-separation burdens read.
sources.use: CO2 recovery and oxygen supply require full process costs; lower dry CO2 fraction alone does not establish the lunar capture penalty.
